outcomes.original: Filing step: If formula retail, file a Conditional Use Authorization application with San Francisco Planning under Section 303, including the building permit plans, a formula retail findings package, and proof of a pre-application community meeting. What to say: Emphasize that this is an enlargement of an existing restaurant that has operated at this location since 2003, not a new use. Frame the project as enhancing an established neighborhood business by improving the facilities and bathrooms, and merging storefronts to create a more efficient layout. Address the formula retail findings under Section 303.1: the chain serves sustainably sourced seafood, employs local staff, and fits the neighborhood's dining character. Note that the use is principally permitted and the only issue is formula retail status. Request that the Commission approve the CUA with standard bona fide eating place conditions and no additional restrictions.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File the building permit application with DBI for tenant improvements, structural work, and bathroom upgrades, routing through Planning as an agency referral. What to say: State that this is an enlargement of the existing Pacific Catch restaurant by merging storefronts within the same parcel (2015-2027 Chestnut St), with structural work, bathroom improvements, and no change to the restaurant use or alcohol service. Note that the space has operated as a restaurant since 2003 with an active Type 41 ABC license and health permit. If Planning has issued a written determination that this is not formula retail, attach it to the building permit application and request expedited routing as a continuation of use. If formula retail CUA is required, note that the building permit is contingent on CUA approval and coordinate the DBI and Planning timelines.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Schedule the DPH pre-final inspection at 80% construction completion and the final inspection at least two weeks before the target opening date, after the building permit final is issued. What to say: Confirm with the DPH plan reviewer that all equipment, finishes, and surfaces match the approved plans, and that a certified food safety manager is on staff (required within 60 days of opening). Walk the space against the DPH checklist one week before the inspection to ensure hand sinks, hot water, sealed surfaces, and the grease interceptor are installed and functional. After the final inspection passes, the DPH permit to operate will be issued and the restaurant can serve the public in the enlarged space.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $5,000 to $20,000. Notes: Time to approval: 120–300 days for a Conditional Use Authorization (if formula retail is confirmed) plus building permit, DPH plan check, and health permit to operate. The CUA accounts for 90–180 days (pre-application meeting, environmental review, hearing scheduling, 30-day appeal period). Building permit review adds 14–60 days after CUA approval, and DPH plan check and final inspection add 21–60 days. If Planning determines this is not formula retail, the timeline drops to 50–120 days (building permit, DPH plan check, and final inspection only, routed as agency referrals). Government costs: CUA application fee $3,100–$6,000 (depending on construction valuation and fee waivers), building permit $800–$15,000 (percentage of construction cost), DPH plan check $828–$2,500 (flat fee for remodel), health permit to operate $470 (FY2026–27 fee). Total government cost range assumes CUA is required; if not, subtract the CUA fee.
